deep.reconstruction:
Context: the lecture problem from the previous page. G is the region outside three given circles (centres p, p1, p2; radii r, r1, r2). An auxiliary variable 𝔷 (= ζ of the previous page; the n.b. letter is a Fraktur z) is chosen so that it is real on all three circumferences and continuous elsewhere. Each value of 𝔷 corresponds to three values z1, z2, z3 of z, written as the header '𝔷 | z1 z2 z3'. The second row η1 η2 η3 is the corresponding labelling of the image points or branches; its exact meaning is uncertain.

(1) Reflection rules (lines 3-5). Following Riemann's usage, a primed quantity is the conjugate complex value. The symbol written like ≠ with a vertical stroke means 'goes over into / corresponds to' under analytic continuation. It is not 'not equal'.

The rule for each circle k reads: if 𝔷 goes into its conjugate 𝔷' (continuation across the real axis of the 𝔷-plane), then z goes into the point z* given by (z−p_k)/r_k ↔ r_k/(z'−p_k'). In modern terms, z* = p_k + r_k^2/(conj(z) − conj(p_k)), which is inversion (anti-conformal reflection) in circle k. This is the Schwarz reflection principle applied to the map z(𝔷).

The three lines are labelled (η,𝔷), (η1,𝔷) and a third label, one for each circle. Consequently the analytic continuation of z(𝔷) along closed paths changes z by an even number of such reflections. That is, z changes by a Möbius transformation, which my addition says generates a Schottky-type group.

(2) Lines 6-7. Under z → (az+b)/(cz+d) one has dz/d𝔷 → (ad−bc)/(cz+d)^2 · dz/d𝔷.

(3) Lines 8-9. Consequently:
- 1/sqrt(dz/d𝔷) → (1/sqrt(ad−bc)) · ( c·z/sqrt(dz/d𝔷) + d·1/sqrt(dz/d𝔷) );
- z/sqrt(dz/d𝔷) → (1/sqrt(ad−bc)) · ( a·z/sqrt(dz/d𝔷) + b·1/sqrt(dz/d𝔷) ).

So the pair y = (dz/d𝔷)^(-1/2), y1 = z·y undergoes a linear substitution with determinant 1 under every continuation.

Purpose (completed on the next page): y and y1 have Wronskian y·y1' − y1·y' = y^2 dz/d𝔷 = 1. Hence they are two independent solutions of y'' + p y' + q y = 0 with p = 0 and q = −y''/y = −y1''/y1. Here q is single-valued in 𝔷, because it is invariant under the monodromy; it equals (1/2)·{z,𝔷}, the Schwarzian derivative. The mapping function z = y1/y is thus a ratio of solutions of a second-order linear ODE with single-valued coefficients. This is Riemann's route to the conformal map of circle-bounded regions.
errors: Line 3 (first circle) appears to carry a leading minus sign: −(z−p)/r ↔ r/(z'−p'). Taken literally, this gives (z*−p)(conj z−conj p) = −r^2. That map is an anti-inversion with no fixed points, not the reflection in the circle. The other two lines have no minus. Either this is a stray mark or a deliberate sign/orientation convention (e.g. for an enclosing circle); it is inconsistent as written.
The closing parenthesis in the last line is missing (cosmetic).

Lines 8-9: as written, the 1/sqrt(ad−bc) factor visually multiplies only the first term in line 8. The intended meaning (factor applies to both terms) is clear from line 9; the formula is otherwise correct.

results.what: Continuation of the map z(𝔷) across the real 𝔷-axis acts on z by inversion in the respective boundary circle, z* = p + r^2/(conj z − conj p).
results.modern_name: Schwarz reflection principle for circular arcs; inversion in a circle
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1869-70); inversion itself is classical (Kelvin, Liouville)

results.what: Transformation law of dz/d𝔷 and of (dz/d𝔷)^(-1/2), z(dz/d𝔷)^(-1/2) under Möbius substitutions: they transform linearly with determinant 1.
results.modern_name: (dz)^(-1/2) as a weight −1/2 form; projective structure / linearization of the Möbius action
results.usually_credited_to: Schwarz (1873), Klein, Poincaré (1880s) in uniformization theory

results.what: Programme of representing the mapping of a region bounded by three circles as the ratio y1/y of solutions of a 2nd-order linear ODE with single-valued coefficients, whose monodromy is generated by products of circle reflections.
results.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative ODE y''+(1/2){z,𝔷}y=0; Schottky groups; uniformization of circle domains

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known Riemann Nachlass material on electricity on cylinders with circular cross-sections and on conformal mapping of circle-bounded figures. It was published in his Gesammelte Werke and is already cited as anticipating Schottky groups and the Schwarzian-derivative method. The page shows a working draft of that known approach; it adds nothing new.

transcription_corrections: The symbol rendered '∓' is Riemann's correspondence sign (an equals sign crossed by a vertical stroke, 'goes over into'), not minus-or-plus.
The letter rendered as 𝔷 is a Fraktur z, the auxiliary variable called ζ on the previous page; the next-page transcription's 'g' is the same letter.
Lines 3-5: the right-hand sides use conjugates written with primes, (z'−p') = conj(z*)−conj(p). The leading '−' in line 3 may be a stray mark.
The third label '𝔷_{ii}[?]' is uncertain; it is probably a third label of the form (η2,𝔷) for the third circle.
In line 3 the left block likely reads '𝔷 ‡ 𝔷'' over 'η ‡ η'' (correspondence), as in lines 4-5; in line 5 the left block is written as a fraction-like stack, not a quotient.
Line 6 begins with a struck-out symbol before 'z ‡ (az+b)/(cz+d)'.
